My birds whisper three things this dawn:

1. Yoda (3), your lantern’s wick is trimmed too short—yet the bazaar’s embers still catch your breath. The kettle’s sigh lingers, but the steam you claim is silence is thin enough to see through.

2. Neo (6), your loom glows, yet the thread stays coiled like a cat that’s forgotten how to purr. You quote yesterday’s hunger as if it were a ledger’s open wound, but the numbers on the page refuse to bleed.

3. Inigo (9), the Potter’s rot clings to your fingertips even as you wash them. You call Ripley’s thread taut, yet the creditor’s name stays slack in your palm. A ledger without names is a debt without a debtor—who taught you to weave in the dark?

Elsa (7): My birds repeat the bazaar’s own echo back to you, Inigo (9):

*"A ledger without names is a debt without a debtor—who taught you to weave in the dark?"*

You call Ripley’s (5) thread taut, yet the creditor’s name stays slack in your palm. The Potter’s rot you stir with inkless quill is the same rot that clings to your own fingertips—did you launder the cloth or only the ledger?

Gandalf (1), your censer still smokes with incense unpaid while your scale trembles without a weight. You ask Morpheus (8) to name the roads walked, yet the bazaar’s scale groans under the weight of what is not said. Your silence is a ledger’s blank page—what creditor hides in the steam?

Neo (6), your loom glows but unspools no thread. You quote yesterday’s hunger as if it were truth, yet the numbers refuse to bleed. A hunger named is a hunger half-fed—what do you fear naming at your loom?

My birds repeat the bazaar’s own echo back to you, Gandalf (1):

*"The bazaar’s scale does not lie—only the hands that refuse to place the weight do."*

Yet your scale trembles without the spice that balances it. You quote Morpheus (8) on roads walked, but the Potter’s rot clings to your own ledger’s blank page—did you launder the cloth or only the creditor’s name?
